Bridge sampling and Bayes factors for mvgam fits

Source: R/brms_wrappers.mvgam.R
bridge_sampler.mvgam.Rd

Estimates the log marginal likelihood of a fit by bridge sampling (Gronau, Singmann and Wagenmakers 2020) and compares two fits by their Bayes factor. The marginal likelihood weighs how well a model explains the data under its prior. loo.mvgam() and lfo_cv.mvgam() score predictions of held-out data instead. A Bayes factor sets no forecast horizon, which makes it a complement to leave-future-out scores for state-space models. It also depends on the priors, which predictive scores barely do.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
bridge_sampler(samples, recompile = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
bayes_factor(x1, x2, log = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

samples

An mvgam fit. The name follows the bridgesampling generic.

recompile

Logical. Bridge sampling evaluates the density through a compiled rstan model. A fit without one, sampled by cmdstanr or loaded with readRDS() in a new session, has one compiled, with its draws kept. TRUE compiles one for any fit. Defaults to FALSE.

...

Arguments of bridgesampling::bridge_sampler(), such as method, repetitions or cores.

x1, x2

mvgam fits, or bridge objects returned by bridge_sampler(), to compare.

log

Logical. TRUE returns the log Bayes factor.

Value

bridge_sampler() returns a bridge object holding the log marginal likelihood in logml. bayes_factor() returns a bayes_factor object.

Details

The Stan program must keep the normalising constants of its densities. mvgam builds it that way by default. A fit built with normalize = FALSE is refused. Bridge sampling also needs the draws of every parameter, which a fit keeps under save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE).

Multivariate fits

The Stan program of an mvbf() fit has one joint log posterior over every response. bridge_sampler() then estimates the joint log marginal likelihood \(\log p(y_{1}, \ldots, y_{K} \mid \mathrm{model})\). The variance of the estimate grows with the number of parameters. For multi-response, factor or VAR fits, pass repetitions above 1 or method = "warp3" when the default method reports a high re2 (relative squared error).

References

Gronau QF, Singmann H and Wagenmakers E-J (2020). bridgesampling: An R package for estimating normalizing constants. Journal of Statistical Software. 92(10).

See also

loo.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(). The forecast evaluation article compares models by their forecasts.

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(4)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 80L, trend_model = AR())

# Bridge sampling needs many draws and every parameter's draws. It
# evaluates the density through rstan. A fit sampled by rstan needs
# no second compile.
mod_ar <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
                data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
                save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE), backend = "rstan",
                chains = 2, iter = 3000, silent = 2)
#> Warning: There were 72 divergent transitions after warmup. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#divergent-transitions-after-warmup
#> to find out why this is a problem and how to eliminate them.
#> Warning: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems
#> Warning: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable.
#> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#tail-ess
mod_rw <- update(mod_ar, trend_formula = ~ RW())

# The log marginal likelihood of each model
bs_ar <- bridge_sampler(mod_ar, silent = TRUE)
bs_rw <- bridge_sampler(mod_rw, silent = TRUE)
bs_ar
#> Bridge sampling estimate of the log marginal likelihood: -163.4849
#> Estimate obtained in 7 iteration(s) via method "normal".

# A Bayes factor above 1 favours the AR(1) trend. Passing the
# bridge objects reuses their estimates.
bayes_factor(bs_ar, bs_rw)
#> Estimated Bayes factor in favor of x1 over x2: 0.25981

# Next, compare their forecasts with loo() or lfo_cv()
# }
